title: Identification and genetic characterization of Saprolegnia parasitica, isolated from farmed and wild fish in Finland
rationale: Both role allocations were acceptable; prefer epidemiology as primary and diagnosis/detection as secondary.

title: Evaluation of different dietary protein sources on tissue growth and metabolism of rainbow trout
rationale: Growth and metabolism are explicit substantive outcomes, not incidental measurements. Prefer Pass A.

title: Growth of farmed blue mussels (Mytilus edulis L.) in a Norwegian coastal area; comparison of food proxies by DEB modeling
rationale: Ontology re-audit: V3_005 remains PRIMARY because release/fate/effects of salmon feed and faecal waste are a central study objective; V3_110 and V3_043 are also PRIMARY; V3_020 SECONDARY; exclude V3_044.

title: Changes in the EPA and DHA content and lipids quality parameters of rainbow trout at individual stages of hot smoking
rationale: EPA/DHA and lipid-quality changes are an explicit co-primary object of the smoking study. Prefer Pass A.

title: Pathology of amoebic gill disease in Atlantic Salmon (Salmo salar L.)
rationale: Ontology re-audit: disease pathology remains PRIMARY; anatomy/tissues is SECONDARY because lesion morphology and histopathological tissue changes are substantive objectives, not incidental sampling; diagnosis/detection and water/ocean conditions remain SECONDARY.

title: Salmon mortalities associated with a bloom of Alexandrium fundyense in 2003 in the Bay of Fundy, and subsequent early warning approaches for industry
rationale: Mortality is a substantive consequence of the bloom and motivates the monitoring programme. Prefer Pass B.

title: MODELLING ANIMAL SYSTEMS PAPER Adaptation of a non-ruminant nutrient-based growth model to rainbow trout
rationale: Growth and physiology are modelled/validation outcomes; methodological development is the principal contribution. Prefer Pass A.

title: Marine growth and morphometrics for three populations of Atlantic salmon from Eastern Maine, USA
rationale: Growth and morphology are both explicit substantive study objectives. Prefer Pass A; Pass B is a low-cost role difference.

title: Cuidando la Patagonia Azul: Prácticas y estrategias de los pueblos originarios para curar las zonas marinas del sur de Chile
rationale: Indigenous rights/governance and livelihoods are central; Indigenous knowledge is a substantive secondary theme. Neither pass alone was complete.

title: Atypical Aeromonas salmonicida vapA type V and Vibrio spp. are predominant bacteria recovered from ballan wrasse Labrus bergylta in Scotland
rationale: Epidemiology is the primary contribution; bacterial identification/characterisation is independently substantive and secondary. Prefer Pass B.

title: Sensitive and rapid detection of infectious pancreatic necrosis virus by reverse transcription loop mediated isothermal amplification
rationale: Method development/validation and IPNV diagnosis/detection are both central contributions. Prefer Pass A; low-cost role disagreement.

title: Life Cycle Considerations for Improving Sustainability Assessments in Seafood Awareness Campaigns
rationale: Life-cycle/environmental assessment is primary; broad environmental impacts and certification/standards are substantive secondary themes. Exclude V3_087 because consumer response to labels is not itself investigated. Prefer Pass B.

title: The Effects of Chilean Coho Salmon and Rainbow Trout Aquaculture on Markets for Alaskan Sockeye Salmon
rationale: Supply, demand and prices are the primary focus; revenues/earnings are explicit modelled outcomes and therefore substantively secondary. Prefer Pass A.

title: Replacement of fish meal with a matrix of organic plant proteins in organic trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) feed, and the effects on nutrient utilization and fish performance
rationale: Alternative feed ingredients and nutrient utilisation are co-primary; growth is substantive secondary; nitrogen/phosphorus outputs are independently substantive environmental outputs. Prefer Pass B.

title: Salmon farming and the environment of the Huon Estuary, Tasmania
rationale: No abstract or DOI available. Do not assign topics from title alone; retrieve abstract/full text before adjudicating V3_001 versus no assignment.

title: A New Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Database for North American Atlantic Salmon Generated Through Whole Genome Resequencing
rationale: No abstract available in the benchmark data. Do not assign V3_051 from title alone; retrieve abstract/full text before adjudication.

title: Big Fish: Valuation of the World’s Largest Salmon Farming Companies
rationale: Pass B best aligns with the ontology: economic valuation is the central appraisal question (V3_027 PRIMARY), and companies are substantive units of analysis (V3_023 SECONDARY). Exclude V3_024 because commercial strategy/business decision-making is not the substantive focus.

title: Effects of two pressed and extruded foods on the pigmentation of the flesh and filleting yield of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss)
rationale: Ontology-first adjudication: preserve shared V3_074, V3_075 and V3_101. V3_097 is substantive but secondary because pigment additives are deliberately tested within whole feed formulations; V3_112 is substantive secondary because growth is explicitly compared; exclude V3_098 because the study does not define nutrient requirements or optimise feed formulation.

title: Simulation models of finfish farms
rationale: Ontology-first adjudication: V3_049 is the central methodological contribution; waste, benthic impacts and water quality are substantive secondary modelled domains. Exclude V3_001 because the ontology directs use of specific environmental pathways when identifiable rather than the broad general-environment code.\n
